newsitem.title: UK: UK tax body calls for fairer, simpler system.
newsitem.headline: UK tax body calls for fairer, simpler system.

text.p: Britain's tax system must be made fairer and simpler for ordinary people to understand, the Chartered Institute of Taxation said on Tuesday.
John Andrews, newly-elected president of the Institute, told its annual meeting that it must bombard the government with suggested reforms to help taxpayers.

"We should press for help for those who cannot afford a tax adviser, in particular the young trying to get into the employment market, the elderly and the unemployed," Andrews said. "Our present tax system is not particularly forgiving for such people and complexity abounds."
On Monday, Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown announced that Martin Taylor, chief executive of Barclays Plc, will spearhead a government drive to modernise Britain's tax and benefit system.
Taylor will lead a Whitehall taskforce aimed at delivering the new government's pledge to "streamline and modernise" the system and to promote incentives to work, the Treasury said.

Social Security Secretary Harriet Harman said the taskforce would explore ways for the tax and benefits system to encourage people to move into work. "We want to tear down the barriers that keep people out of jobs and trapped on benefit," she said. "Work is the best form of welfare for people of working age."

Andrews told the Chartered Institute's annual meeting he expected the government to be sympathetic towards ideas leading to simpler taxation for low level payers, including a reduction in bureaucracy and form-filling. Brown is due to hold a budget within weeks. He has pledged to levy a windfall tax on Britain's privatised utilities, using the proceeds to get 250,000 people into work.
But it is less clear how he will change or simplify the existing tax system. He has promised not to raise the basic rates of income tax or extend the scope of VAT to many areas.
